The clearest favorable evidence is the PACT Act, which he signed to expand veterans’ eligibility for toxic-exposure-related care, together with early federal implementation and screening activity (E014, E024). The administration also supported the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and ordered federal policing reforms addressing accountability, misconduct data, investigations, and use-of-force standards (E007, E009). These are ruler-attributed actions with plausible social-welfare relevance, but their reach and realized effects were limited or unresolved. Independent oversight found that only 79% of surveyed Veterans Health Administration facilities met both mental-health integration requirements, staffing impaired implementation, and VA did not adequately track outside partnerships (E034, E049). REACH VET showed improved appointment completion, but GAO said further impact study was needed (E035). Inflation imposed heavier burdens on lower-income households, although the cited CBO evidence does not establish Biden-specific causation (E023). The record therefore supports genuine federal action and some bounded gains, but not broad, equitable, durable improvement sufficient for a 6.5 or higher; the implementation weaknesses and incomplete The strongest favorable evidence is education reform: government and partners supported the 2022–23 school year, a World Bank-supported program was associated with roughly three million additional enrolled children and about 60,000 teachers added to payroll, and monitoring verified 36,000 teachers added in ten provinces (E016, E043, E054). A named Allo Ecole mechanism accepted complaints about teacher non-payment and abuse with investigation and confidentiality procedures, providing a concrete accountability channel (E045). These gains reflect presidential and government participation, but also substantial donor and provincial involvement. The unfavorable record is broad: approximately 3.2 to 7 million children were out of school under differing denominators, conflict and displacement constrained access, more than 2,000 schools closed, and over 800,000 children were displaced (E017, E044). Free-primary-schooling reform remained unfinished because of insecurity, administrative complexity, and limited assistance (E054), while roughly 5.7 million people were internally displaced by November 2022 (E038). These conditions are not all ruler-caused, but the record shows weak durability, quality, and crisis protection.
